comment.en: Imported category of substantial endurants (objects) whose identity is supplied by their external kinds. It is a bearer anchor, not an additional Riskium domain or a risk case.

A managed, reusable information specification of risk-relevant conditions and possible effects. Its identity is distinct from a particular risk case, a scenario execution and the uncertain effects themselves.
A versioned information specification of analysis boundaries, circumstances, time horizon and objective references under which risk statements and results are interpreted.

A managed information specification of a possible development of conditions, events and effects concerning one or more RiskCases. Several scenarios may concern one case; a scenario is not the case or an actual occurrence.
An actual occurrence or change relevant to a risk scenario; a scenario or report alone does not establish that it happened.
A source-qualified information assertion that possible or reported effects are favorable, unfavorable or mixed relative to identified objectives and context.

A controlled value used to qualify the nature of effects relative to objectives; it does not classify risk independently of context. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A risk-relevant situation that increases susceptibility to specified occurrences or effects. Reference to it requires explicit source support and does not establish a causal mechanism.

An actual occurrence interpreted as initiating a risk-relevant development in a specified context. A hypothetical trigger description is represented as scenario content, not as an actual Trigger individual.

An intrinsic susceptibility of a bearer to specified risk-relevant conditions or effects. The proposed mode interpretation requires a supported bearer; security-specific exploitation meanings remain source-qualified.
A time-qualified situation relating an affected bearer to a risk source or relevant condition. An exposure score or its description is information about that situation.
A temporally qualified state of a risk-relevant situation, distinct from the workflow status of its record.
A managed documentary object with an instituted identity that persists across its descriptions and issued versions. Artifact identity is distinct from a file path, a storage row and semantic content.

An identifiable issued documentary version of a managed information artifact. Its issued semantic content and effective dependency versions are immutable; revisions receive distinct version identities.
The abstract informational meaning expressed by artifacts or versions. Content identity requires an explicit equivalence policy and is not inferred from equal strings or file hashes.

A managed terminological information artifact that identifies a vocabulary meaning independently of its labels. It is a vocabulary resource, not automatically a domain universal or the real-world entity denoted.
A governed organization of classification concepts with an identified scope and version policy.

A managed vocabulary item expressing a controlled classification value within an identified scheme. Scheme membership and version context constrain its interpretation. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A source-qualified assignment of a classification term to a subject in a specified context.
A managed annotation artifact carrying a lightweight label. Identical lexical labels do not by themselves identify one tag assignment or imply a formal taxonomy.

A managed register record about exactly one RiskCase in this profile. Distinct entries, source systems or registers can record the same case. A software record is an implementation record, not an additional risk subject.
An identifiable version of a register entry, preserving the content and qualified links effective at its issue.
A descriptive information item about a risk case, pattern or scenario with an explicit description role and source.
An information item expressing a possible or reported consequence; it is not the consequence itself.
Recorded information about identifying a risk, including the stated source, channel, agent and available time information.
A controlled value naming how risk information entered the registration process; it is not a risk source. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A controlled value specifying the function of a description, such as title, summary or scenario description. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A controlled value preserving the source-defined position or role of a consequence statement. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

A managed informational register that organizes risk-entry records for a stated organizational scope and purpose. Its documentary identity does not make it an OntoUML collective or physical aggregate.

An actual activity contributing to risk identification, analysis or evaluation. It may cover only part of a risk assessment; the complete standardized assessment process is outside the current process-modeling scope.
A managed information artifact documenting an assessment and its scope, basis, methods, time context, participants and results. It is distinct from performing that assessment.
A specification of assumptions and control conditions under which an assessment result is interpreted.
A result for one assessment dimension, qualified by its method, scale, basis and relevant temporal context.
A versioned specification of procedures and rules used to produce and interpret assessment results.
A governed scale specification defining permissible values or ordered levels for a specified assessment dimension.
A numeric assessment output produced under a declared scoring method; it is not the risk itself or a universal definition of risk level.
A managed vocabulary resource specifying a permissible value or category on an identified assessment scale version. It denotes a level; it is not a measured value occurrence or a bare lexical label.
A managed vocabulary resource specifying an assessment aspect, such as likelihood or consequence severity. The vocabulary item, the aspect denoted and its measured or judged value remain distinct.

A controlled value indicating the evidential or epistemic character of a result, such as observed, estimated or projected. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A recorded decision about treating risk, including the selected option, rationale, responsible authority and relevant basis.
A controlled value identifying a treatment approach; its selection is represented by a treatment decision. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A versioned specification of intended actions, resources, responsibilities, timing and conditions for a stated purpose.
An actual performance of actions intended to modify or otherwise respond to risk, distinct from the plan describing them.
A controlled value describing the role of a plan, such as primary response or contingency. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
An entity capable of performing or being accountable for relevant actions, including persons and organizations within the declared profile.
A human individual who may participate in risk management activities or assignments.
An organized social entity capable of carrying responsibilities and authorizations in the model's scope.
A source-level identifier or description referring to an actor whose identity may be unresolved.
A recorded statement about an assignment of responsibility or authority, distinct from the relationship it asserts.
A temporally qualified responsibility relationship connecting its participants, responsibility scope and grounding assignment.
A context-dependent role borne by an agent with an assigned responsibility.
A context-dependent role borne by an agent authorized to approve or issue a specified decision or assignment.
A person bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
An organization bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
A person bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
An organization bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
A controlled value identifying the kind of responsibility or authority assigned. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A controlled value describing progress of analysis under a specified analysis-state scheme. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A controlled value describing handling or processing status under a specified workflow scheme. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
A qualified statement about a record's state, preserving the source and available temporal precision.
An issued version of a scheme defining workflow values and permitted transitions.
A temporally bounded situation in which a managed record revision has an assigned workflow state under an identified scheme version; the statement documenting this situation is separate.
A qualified reference linking a claim or activity to an evidence item, with its intended evidential role and provenance.
An information artifact playing an evidential role for a specified claim or analytical activity. The same artifact may be used as evidence in one context and not another.
An activity that observes a stated feature of a subject using a declared procedure and temporal context.
An information result produced by an observation activity, qualified by subject, time, method and available units.
A versioned information specification of an observable or computed indicator, including its intended interpretation. A reported indicator value is an ObservationResult, not the specification.
A versioned information specification of a context-qualified decision boundary for an indicator or assessment scale, with a comparator, permissible value interpretation and applicability context.
An information item indicating a potentially relevant change or condition and potentially prompting review; it does not by itself establish a risk event.
A versioned information specification of reference conditions used to judge the significance or acceptability of risk in an identified context.
A managed, versioned statement recording the kinds and extent of risk an organization is prepared to pursue or retain, qualified by source framework, objectives, authority and context.

A managed, versioned statement recording an organization's stated risk tolerance under an explicitly identified source vocabulary or framework and context. Permissible deviation and readiness to bear remaining risk are retained as distinct source meanings, not silently merged.

An instituted, identifiable subject of enterprise-risk analysis and tracking. It persists across its descriptions, reassessments, responsibilities and administrative record states under a governed identity policy. It is neither its register entry nor a scenario specification nor an actual occurrence.
A managed information item identifying an objective in its source context, without asserting that the information item is the objective.
A managed statement of what is uncertain about a risk case, including assumptions and evidential limitations; it does not imply a numerical probability.
A recorded judgment of risk significance or acceptability based on identified assessment information and criteria versions. It is distinct from a numeric score and from the evaluation activity.
A managed identifier or description of a claimed control whose real-world bearer may remain unresolved.

A managed information artifact identifying or describing a claimed contributor to risk in a declared context. The referenced contributor may be unresolved, hypothetical or heterogeneous. The reference does not establish actual causation or an actual occurrence.
